title: Default tool input sets every schema field to "" and ignores declared defaults
body:
## Summary
buildDefaultInput in ToolInvocationCard pre-fills every property of the tool input_schema with an empty string, whatever its type, and never uses a declared default.

## Description
`src/features/agents/sub_tool_runner/components/ToolInvocationCard.tsx:252-266` loops `Object.keys(schema.properties)` and assigns `defaults[key] = ''`. An integer, boolean or array property therefore starts as a string, and a property with `"default": 10` starts as `""`. The pre-filled payload is valid JSON, so the pre-flight check (`:49-59`) passes and Run is enabled, and the tool receives a type-wrong value. The mcp-tools technique tool-schema-design says "Defaults declared in the schema spare the model a guess it can get wrong"; the human caller here gets the same guess, made wrong for them. Fixed: use `default` when declared, else a type-matched blank (string "", number/integer 0, boolean false, array [], object {}).

## Flow
- a tool whose input_schema has {limit: {type: integer, default: 10}, dry: {type: boolean}}
- expand the card: the textarea reads {"limit": "", "dry": ""}
- press Run without editing: the tool gets limit="" and dry="" (string), not 10 / false

## Expected impact
Pressing Run on an untouched card sends a payload whose types match the tool contract. Could break: nothing; only the initial textarea value changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the default payload matches the declared schema types and defaults
Before: probe (schema q:string, limit:integer default 10, dry:boolean, tags:array): {"q":"","limit":"","dry":"","tags":""} - 3 of 4 keys type-wrong, 1 declared default ignored
After: expected: {"q":"","limit":10,"dry":false,"tags":[]} - 0 type-wrong, 0 defaults ignored
Method: gate - a render test on the card reads the textarea value; red on the unchanged function
Result: better
Gate: none
impact_why: A tool with typed inputs is exercised with wrong types unless the operator rewrites the payload by hand.
predicted_why: no precedent (door decisions empty; none in cycle-1 git)

title: Tool card disclosure button does not expose its expanded state
body:
## Summary
The header button that expands a tool card has no aria-expanded or aria-controls, so assistive tech cannot tell whether the input and Run controls are shown.

## Description
`src/features/agents/sub_tool_runner/components/ToolInvocationCard.tsx:72-95` toggles `expanded` and swaps a ChevronDown/ChevronRight icon; the button carries neither `aria-expanded` nor `aria-controls`, and the body (`:98-167`) has no id. The disclosure pattern needs both. Fixed: `aria-expanded={expanded}`, `aria-controls` pointing at an id on the body.

## Flow
- screen reader focuses the tool card header: announced as "gmail_reader api, button"
- activating it reveals the input, Run and result - nothing announces the change of state

## Expected impact
The header announces collapsed/expanded. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the disclosure exposes its state
Before: probe: toggle.getAttribute("aria-expanded") -> null
After: "false" collapsed, "true" expanded, aria-controls resolves to the body id
Method: gate - render test on the card reads the attribute before and after a click; red today
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/features/agents/sub_tool_runner/components/ToolInvocationCard.tsx:72-77 <button type="button" data-testid={`tool-card-toggle-${tool.name}`} onClick={() => setExpanded(!expanded)} className=...>   // no aria-expanded
probe: aria-expanded: null
impact_why: Every tool card on the runner is a disclosure screen-reader users cannot read the state of.
predicted_why: like 6b646cecd2 (git, decision memory empty), accepted: "mini player Simple-mode progress bar is invisible to assistive tech"

title: Context map describes the retired design wizard and omits four live files
body:
## Summary
The agents-design entry still names DesignTab.tsx and useDesignTabState.ts (deleted 2026-09-04) as entry points, describes the analyzing/refining/preview/applied wizard, and leaves DesignLifePanels, KpRequirementsPanel and kpRequirements unassigned.

## Description
`context-map.json:330-331` lists entry points `src/features/agents/sub_design/DesignTab.tsx` and `src/features/agents/sub_design/libs/useDesignTabState.ts`; neither exists (`src/features/agents/sub_design/index.ts:3-8` records their retirement). The description ("Guides the user through analysis, refining, previewing, and applying phases ... Manages multi-phase state (analyzing, refining, preview, applied, error)") describes the same retired wizard; the hub is now four store-backed sub-tabs (`DesignHub.tsx:44-57`). `file_paths` omits `sub_design/components/DesignLifePanels.tsx` (mounted by DesignHub `:16-24`), `sub_design/components/KpRequirementsPanel.tsx`, `sub_design/libs/kpRequirements.ts` and their tests, so this sweep and every lens keyed on the map never read them. The map is a never-touch surface for this round and an edit to it is an architecture escalation.

## Flow
- a sweep picks agents-design and reads its 10 file_paths
- DesignLifePanels (three of the four sub-tabs) and the kp-requirements pair are never read
- the next context scan should re-judge the entry; or an operator patches the entry

## Expected impact
The map routes the files the hub actually mounts to this context. Could break: context reassignment shifts coverage history.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the map entry resolves to live files and covers what the hub mounts
Before: entry points resolving: 1 of 3; sibling source files in sub_design not in any context: 3
After: 3 of 3; 0 unassigned
Method: probe - ls of each named path and grep of context-map.json for the three files (0 hits)
Result: better
Gate: architecture - an edit to the context map
evidence:
context-map.json:330-331 "src/features/agents/sub_design/DesignTab.tsx", "src/features/agents/sub_design/libs/useDesignTabState.ts" (ls: no such file)
$ grep -n "KpRequirementsPanel\|kpRequirements.ts\|DesignLifePanels" context-map.json -> (none)
src/features/agents/sub_design/DesignHub.tsx:16-24 lazyRetry(() => import('./components/DesignLifePanels') ...)
impact_why: Three of the hub's four sub-tab mounts are outside every context, so sweeps and scoped agents never read them.
predicted_why: no precedent (door decisions empty; none in cycle-1 git); c39ba683e5 refreshed the map deterministically and did not re-judge this entry

title: Tool card offers Run on tools the backend can only reject
body:
## Summary
ToolInvocationCard classifies a tool from category and script_path alone, so a tool with no execution strategy shows as "api" and one with both script and API guide shows as "script" - both get a Run button that can only fail.

## Description
The backend decides a tool kind in `src-tauri/core/src/models/tool.rs:106-127` (`tool_kind`): automation by category, else script XOR implementation_guide; both set is an error ("conflicting execution strategies") and neither is an error ("no execution strategy"). The card mirrors only half of it at `src/features/agents/sub_tool_runner/components/ToolInvocationCard.tsx:38-41`: builtin, automation, `script_path ? script : api`. It never reads `implementation_guide`, so the two error cases are offered a Run that returns a failure every time. The builtin case already got the honest treatment for the same reason (comment at `:35-37`, 2026-07-16 UAT: a Run that can only fail "read as my persona is broken"). Fixed: derive the card kind with the backend rule and show a note instead of Run for the two unrunnable shapes.

## Flow
- a tool row with script_path "" and no implementation_guide (or both set)
- expand its card: chip reads "api" (or "script") and Run is enabled
- press Run: invoke_tool_direct returns success:false "no execution strategy" every time

## Expected impact
A misconfigured tool says so before the operator spends a run on it. Could break: a tool whose implementation_guide is set and empty string is treated as no guide, matching the backend.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the card offers Run on exactly the tools the backend can run
Before: probe: tool {script_path:"", implementation_guide:null} -> Run offered, chip "api"; kind rules agreeing with tool_kind: 3 of 5 shapes (builtin, automation, script-only, api-only agree; none / both disagree)
After: 5 of 5; the two unrunnable shapes show a note and no Run button
Method: gate - render test on the card for the no-strategy and both-strategy shapes, red today
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/features/agents/sub_tool_runner/components/ToolInvocationCard.tsx:39-41
  const toolType = isBuiltin ? 'builtin' : tool.category === 'automation' ? 'automation' : tool.script_path ? 'script' : 'api';
src-tauri/core/src/models/tool.rs:115-125 (true,true) => Err("conflicting execution strategies") ... (false,false) => Err("no execution strategy")
probe: no-strategy Run offered: true chip: pingapi
impact_why: Only misconfigured tool rows are affected, but there the runner reports a broken persona instead of a broken tool row.
predicted_why: like the builtin-honesty fix recorded at ToolInvocationCard.tsx:35-37 (2026-07-16 UAT, in-code); door decisions empty, none in cycle-1 git

title: Tool run result appears without a live-region announcement
body:
## Summary
When a direct tool run settles, the success/failure block is inserted silently; a screen-reader user who pressed Run hears nothing.

## Description
`ResultDisplay` (`src/features/agents/sub_tool_runner/components/ToolInvocationCard.tsx:172-250`) mounts a new block on settle with no `role="status"`/`aria-live` on it or on a stable container. The Run button announces its loading label (`:155-156`) and then simply re-enables. Fixed: a stable `aria-live="polite"` wrapper around the result slot (or `role="status"` on the result header; `role="alert"` on the error variant).

## Flow
- screen reader: press Run; "Running..." is announced
- the call settles: the result block appears; nothing is announced

## Expected impact
The outcome of a run is announced. Could break: verbose announcements if the whole output pre sits inside the live region - wrap the header only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a settled run is announced
Before: live regions on the result path: 0
After: 1 (status for success/failure, alert for an IPC error)
Method: gate - render test asserts getByRole("status") contains the Success/Failed label after a result; red today
Result: better
Gate: none
impact_why: Screen-reader users must hunt for the outcome of every run.
predicted_why: like 6b646cecd2 (git, decision memory empty), accepted: "progress bar is invisible to assistive tech"

title: useSavedDesignResult Google OAuth fixup has no test
body:
## Summary
The only logic in designStateHelpers - stamping oauth_type "google" on gmail / google_calendar / google_drive connectors that lack one - is pinned by no test.

## Description
`src/features/agents/sub_design/libs/designStateHelpers.ts:15-32` parses `last_design_result` and rewrites `suggested_connectors` for three Google names. No test file references `useSavedDesignResult` or `designStateHelpers` (grep over `src/**/*.test.*`: 0). The DesignConnectorsToolRunner harness stubs the recap, so the rewritten connectors never reach an assertion. A rename of a Google connector, or a reorder that drops the `!c.oauth_type` guard (overwriting an explicit oauth_type), passes every gate. Fixed: a renderHook test covering parse failure -> null, a Google connector without oauth_type -> google, one with an explicit oauth_type kept, a non-Google connector untouched.

## Flow
- seed: delete the !c.oauth_type guard in the helper
- today: no test fails; with the instrument: the "explicit oauth_type kept" case goes red

## Expected impact
The fixup cannot regress silently. Could break: nothing (test only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the helper's four behaviours are pinned
Before: cases pinned: 0 of 4 (grep: no test references the helper)
After: 4 of 4; seeded mutation (guard removed) goes red
Method: gate - write the renderHook test, seed the mutation, watch it go red
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/features/agents/sub_design/libs/designStateHelpers.ts:19-27 const GOOGLE_CONNECTORS = new Set(['gmail', 'google_calendar', 'google_drive']); ... !c.oauth_type && GOOGLE_CONNECTORS.has(c.name) ? { ...c, oauth_type: 'google' as const } : c
$ grep -rln "useSavedDesignResult\|designStateHelpers" src --include=*.test.* -> (none)
impact_why: Small helper, but the only place Google connectors in an old design get their OAuth flow.
predicted_why: like d422866d3b (git, decision memory empty), accepted: "fake-timer instrument for a digest that becomes due while the app stays open" - a test-only instrument commit

title: DesignHub declares four props it never reads, one no caller passes
body:
## Summary
DesignHub takes draft, patch, modelDirty and onConnectorsMissingChange and binds none of them; EditorBody threads the first three for nothing and nobody passes the fourth, whose comment claims EditorBody needs it.

## Description
`src/features/agents/sub_design/DesignHub.tsx:29-35` declares the props and `:69` takes them as `_props` (unbound). The doc comment at `:33` says `onConnectorsMissingChange` is "Retained for the EditorBody contract", but `src/features/agents/sub_editor/components/EditorBody.tsx:197-201` passes only `draft`, `patch`, `modelDirty` (grep for `onConnectorsMissingChange` in src: the declaration only). The draft/patch threading forces EditorBody to pass editor state into a component that reads the store instead (comment `:62-68`). Fixed: drop `onConnectorsMissingChange` (in scope, XS) and the three unused props with their call site (EditorBody, another context).

## Flow
- grep onConnectorsMissingChange: 1 hit (the declaration)
- EditorBody:197 passes draft/patch/modelDirty; DesignHub binds none

## Expected impact
The Design hub contract says what it uses. Could break: nothing at runtime; a type change at one call site.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - declared-but-unread props drop from 4 to 0
Before: unread props: 4; props whose comment claims a caller that does not exist: 1
After: 0 and 0; tsc exit 0
Method: probe - grep + read of the one call site; the full fix crosses into sub_editor (out of scope)
Result: better
Gate: none
impact_why: Misleading contract on the editor's main tab; a comment names a caller that does not exist.
predicted_why: like 8098359bfd (git, decision memory empty), accepted: "drop the parseFeasibilityToHealthResult withProposals option"
instrument: npx tsc --noEmit exit 0 on both arms + grep count of unread DesignHub props 4 -> 0

title: useToolRunner writes two user-facing errors as hardcoded English
body:
## Summary
The tool-runner hook puts "No active persona. Open a persona before running tools." and "Tool invocation failed" into the card's error slot as literals instead of catalog keys.

## Description
`src/features/agents/sub_tool_runner/libs/useToolRunner.ts:69` and `:109` are user-facing - `ResultDisplay` prints `error` verbatim (`src/features/agents/sub_tool_runner/components/ToolInvocationCard.tsx:184`). `.claude/CLAUDE.md` requires every user-facing string through `t`; the lint rule `custom/no-hardcoded-jsx-text` only sees JSX, so a hook literal escapes it. The no-persona branch is unreachable from the only mount (Design -> Connectors renders the runner only with a selected persona, `DesignSubtabPanels.tsx:97-106`), so the live exposure is the fallback string on a rejection with no extractable message. Fixed: two keys under `agents.tool_runner` and `useTranslation` in the hook.

## Flow
- a direct run rejects with an object extractMessage cannot read
- the card shows the literal "Tool invocation failed"

## Expected impact
All tool-runner copy lives in the catalog. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - hardcoded user-facing literals in the context drop to zero
Before: hardcoded user-facing literals in useToolRunner.ts: 2 (lines 69, 109)
After: 0
Method: probe - grep count on the file; a test would assert the catalog value
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/features/agents/sub_tool_runner/libs/useToolRunner.ts:69  error: 'No active persona. Open a persona before running tools.',
src/features/agents/sub_tool_runner/libs/useToolRunner.ts:109 const msg = extractMessage(err) || 'Tool invocation failed';
impact_why: English-only product today and one string is unreachable from the live mount; convention debt.

title: Ten catalog keys under design_subtabs and tool_runner have no reader
body:
## Summary
Eight agents.design_subtabs keys (the retired sub-tabs) and two agents.tool_runner keys (run_tool, failure_kind_label) are read by nothing after the 2026-09-04 hub collapse.

## Description
DesignHub reads `design_subtabs` only through `SUB_TABS[].labelKey` (manifest, responsibilities, brain, connectors - `src/features/agents/sub_design/DesignHub.tsx:52-57`, `:91`) and DesignSubtabPanels reads `.connectors` (`:91`). The catalog still carries `use_cases`, `prompt`, `parameters`, `triggers`, `messaging`, `core`, `triggers_desc`, `messaging_desc` (`src/i18n/locales/en.json:3083-3096`). In `tool_runner`, `run_tool` and `failure_kind_label` (`en.json:5084`, `:5090`) have no reader. Zero-consumer grep for each key (direct and bracket access) returns 0. Fixed: purge them through the repo tool (`scripts/i18n/purge-dead-keys.mjs`) so all 14 locale files and the generated types move together.

## Flow
- grep each key across src (excluding generated): 0 readers for all ten
- run purge-dead-keys over the ten; regenerate i18n types; tsc green

## Expected impact
Translators and the catalog stop carrying copy for screens that do not exist. Could break: a dynamic reader the grep missed - the purge tool and tsc on generated types catch it.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - dead keys in these two sections drop from 10 to 0
Before: dead keys: 10 (grep: 0 readers each)
After: 0, with tsc exit 0 on regenerated types
Method: probe - per-key grep; the purge touches 14 locale files and generated types (shared surface, other sessions merge into it)
Result: better
Gate: none
